input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 conditions our ability to engage any other provider on first disclosing and matching for Vendor any more favourable offer we receive. That is a de facto exclusivity / right-of-first-refusal binding the Customer: it applies to all Services, for the entire term, with no product-category limit, no 12-month sunset, and no automatic exit for Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates, so it fails the fallback and sits in walk-away territory (exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit). It also directly contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment. Preferred remedy is deletion. The Section 2.1 take-or-pay minimum volume and the Section 12.4 non-compete are separate commercial terms addressed under their own rules and are not double-flagged here.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the requirement to disclose and match third-party offers before engaging another provider: it operates as a de facto exclusivity/right of first refusal on us, and our playbook does not accept exclusivity or sole-supplier obligations on the customer. It also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity commitment. If Vendor needs something here, we could consider a narrow exclusivity limited to a defined service category, capped at twelve months and ending automatically if Vendor misses a service level or delivery date.
proposal.summary: Delete Section 7.2 disclose-and-match obligation (de facto exclusivity/ROFR on Customer).
